stem: What four sequential phases make up the strategic implementation approach recommended by the W3C Web Accessibility Initiative (WAI)?

options.rationale: This sequence describes a technical accessibility audit and remediation pipeline, rather than the comprehensive organizational management framework defined by W3C WAI.
The W3C WAI 'Planning and Managing Web Accessibility' framework structures enterprise-wide accessibility adoption into these four distinct organizational phases.
This represents the Deming Cycle (PDCA) commonly used in general ISO quality management, not the strategic organizational roadmap formulated by the W3C.
This sequence represents a standard software development lifecycle (SDLC) or UX design process, rather than the W3C's enterprise governance framework.

explanation: The World Wide Web Consortium's Web Accessibility Initiative (W3C WAI) provides guidance in 'Planning and Managing Web Accessibility' structured into four strategic phases: (1) Initiate—gathering support, learning basics, and defining vision; (2) Plan—establishing accessibility policies, budgeting, and assigning roles; (3) Implement—training staff, procuring accessible tools, and integrating accessibility into everyday development; and (4) Sustain—continually monitoring conformance, engaging with users with disabilities, and adapting processes over time.

references.title: Web Accessibility Initiative: Planning and Managing Web Accessibility
